title: A stretchable, electroconductive tissue adhesive for the treatment of neural injury

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods section 2.2, Equation (1) for degree of methacrylation
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The formula DM = (integrated area of methacrylate protons) / (integrated area of reference peak × number of protons in methacrylate group) is dimensionally and chemically wrong. Degree of methacrylation should normalize the methacrylate integral by the number of methacrylate protons and normalize the reference integral by the number of reference protons, then multiply by 100. The equation omits the reference-proton count and percent factor and places the methacrylate proton count in the denominator.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods section 2.2 / Results section 3.1, NMR reference peak assigned to tryptophan
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper describes the custom ELP sequence as ([VPGVG]4[IPGVG])14 with a lysine-cysteine-threonine-serine sequence, which contains no tryptophan residue. Yet the DM calculation uses an aromatic peak at 7.5 ppm attributed to Trp (W) as the reference. This is internally inconsistent unless a Trp residue is present but it is not described.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results section 3.1, Bio-IL NMR peak assignment
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states the sharp peak at δ ~ 3.1 ppm corresponds to 'the three hydrogen atoms of the ammonium ion.' Choline is (2-hydroxyethyl)trimethylammonium with an N+(CH3)3 group, which has nine equivalent methyl protons, not three.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results section 3.1, description of reactive groups and disulfide formation
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says 'mELP chains containing photoreactive methacrylate and cystine groups formed new covalent carbon–carbon (−C−C−) and disulfide (−S−S−) bonds.' Cystine is the disulfide product of two cysteine residues; the reactive side chain in the ELP is cysteine with a thiol group. Conflating cysteine with cystine is a chemical error.

predicted_errors.error_location: Figure 2 caption vs Statistical analysis section 2.11
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The statistical analysis section states 'error bars were evaluated as the mean ± standard deviation (SD)', but the Figure 2 caption states 'error bars indicate the standard error of the means'. These are different measures and the paper inconsistently reports which was used.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods section 2.8, ex vivo electrical conduction experiment
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The ex vivo muscle stimulation protocol says electric pulses were applied from a 'voltage source (potentiostat; Agilent, 4284A)'. The Agilent 4284A is a precision LCR meter, not a potentiostat or a pulse stimulator for applying 50 ms electrical pulses to tissue. The stated instrumentation cannot perform the described stimulation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results section 3.1 / Figure 2c, claimed NMR confirmation of disulfide bonds
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims multiplet peaks between 1.0 and 1.1 ppm 'confirmed the formation of disulfide (−S−S−) bonds' in the crosslinked hydrogel. 1H NMR cannot directly detect a disulfide bond because it contains no protons, and a generic multiplet around 1.0–1.1 ppm is not a specific diagnostic for disulfide formation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and Conclusions/title claims of neural injury treatment and regeneration
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The title and abstract claim the material enables 'sutureless surgical sealing of neural injuries and promote tissue regeneration' and 'treatment of neural injury'. However, the reported experiments include only material characterization, glial cell viability, ex vivo muscle conduction, and subcutaneous implantation in rats. No nerve injury model, nerve repair outcome, or nerve regeneration data are presented, so the therapeutic/regenerative claims are unsupported.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods section 2.7, wound closure/adhesion testing compared with Evicel
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract claims adhesive strength '~10 times higher than commercially available tissue adhesive, Evicel®', but the Materials section describes only wound-closure testing on rat peripheral nerve using the mELP/Bio-IL prepolymer and provides no protocol for preparing or testing Evicel as a comparator. A quantitative comparative claim requires a described comparison method.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods section 2.10, in vivo study design
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The in vivo study used a total of two rats, one euthanized at day 7 and one at day 28, and states 'For each group, four samples were tested.' This means the four samples per group at each time point came from the same animal, so they are not independent biological replicates. Any statistical treatment of these samples as independent replicates would be pseudoreplication.
